top_story: After two months of confrontation set off by Trump’s threat to destroy Iran’s power infrastructure unless Tehran reopened the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran is now signaling a draft framework with Washington that would restore commercial shipping and end the U.S. naval blockade. The reported partial easing of Iran’s internet blackout suggests the de-escalation is not only maritime but domestic, offering limited relief after a period shaped by coercion and regional escalation threats. On the same day, Israeli settlers backed by soldiers raided villages north of Ramallah, killed 16-year-old Yousef Kaabneh, and seized roughly 900 sheep, underscoring how violence in the occupied West Bank continues to deepen dispossession even as one major regional flashpoint cools. The emerging picture is of a region where crisis management between states can reduce immediate strategic risk without easing the daily insecurity imposed on civilians under occupation.
